purpose: Teach: 暑かっ/お便り/大通り/用心/台無し/音読/円形/探究

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃の夏、本気で、暑かったよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?エアコン、なかった時代、絶対、大変だった、本気で、本当に。
lines.en: The summers when I was young—they were brutally hot, weren't they? Do you remember, dear? The days before air conditioning. It must have been absolutely difficult.
lines.style: Slow, measured opening. Voice trails into memory. Slight pause mid-sentence, as if watching the past. Gentle, nostalgic exhale. No hurry to finish.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。息子から、お便り、本気で、本当に、嬉しいわよね、覚えてる?あなた、本気で、絶対、毎月、楽しみにしていたわね。
lines.en: Yes. I do remember. Letters from our son—they made me so happy. Every single month, I looked forward to them, you know?
lines.style: Warm agreement, voice softens at 'letters.' Brief pause to let the memory settle. Then a little brightness creeps in. Speaking to him across years, not just across the room.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、大通り、本気で、人通り、多かったわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で、本当に、にぎやかな、時代、絶対。
lines.en: The big avenue in those days—so many people passing by. Do you remember, dear? It was truly lively then. A different time.
lines.style: Voice brightens slightly at the memory. Steady pacing, almost cataloguing. Gentle curiosity in the question to her, inviting her back into that time with him.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、最近、本気で、ご用心、しないとね、足元、絶対、危ないわよ、本気で、お互いに、年だしね、絶対、本気。
lines.en: Grandfather, you need to be careful lately. Watch your step—the ground is dangerous for us. We're both getting older, aren't we?
lines.style: Shifts to concerned but steady tone. Not scolding—protecting. A slight firmness under the gentleness, the way she watches him. Matter-of-fact about aging, but the care underneath is clear.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: お祖母ちゃんの、お料理、本気で、台無しに、絶対、しないように、ばあさん、ありがたく、いただこうな、絶対、本気で。
lines.en: Your grandmother's cooking—I mustn't let anything happen to it. Let me receive what she makes with proper gratitude, the way it deserves.
lines.style: Voice becomes quieter, almost reverent. Slow, deliberate pacing. A kind of dedication in the words. Not humble exactly, but acknowledging something precious that shouldn't be wasted.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、二人で、本気で、絶対、音読、よく、したわよね、覚えてる?百人一首、本気で、楽しかったわよ、絶対、本気で。
lines.en: Do you remember when we were young? The two of us reading poetry aloud together—often, wasn't it? The Hundred Poets anthology. How much we enjoyed those times.
lines.style: Brightness returns. Voice has energy now, almost playful in the recall. Rhythm picks up slightly when mentioning the poetry. Genuine delight at the memory, inviting him to feel it again with her.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 家のテーブル、本気で、円形に、絶対、変えたいって、若い頃、夢、見たわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?絶対、本気で、本当に。
lines.en: Our table at home—I remember you wanted so badly to change it to a round one when we were young. You had that dream. Do you remember?
lines.style: Tender curiosity. Voice has a smile in it. Slight tease mixed with genuine affection—she's remembered something he said decades ago. Warm, gentle interrogation.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、本気で、生涯の探究心、本当に、立派、ばあさん、誇りに、絶対、思っているわよ、本気で、感謝、本当に、絶対、本気。
lines.en: Grandfather, your curiosity about life itself—it's been remarkable. I'm truly proud of it. I want you to know how grateful I am for that.
lines.style: Voice becomes earnest and full. Slower pace. Each phrase deliberate, as if telling him something important she's been holding. No performance—direct, deep recognition. Slight catch of emotion but composed.
